Title: Emerging Issue: WA-WebSites:FUNCTIONS Function apps configured to use a separate storage for Durable Functions may not scale properly
Content:
# Emerging Issue Analysis

*Generated on: 2025-05-28 21:10:39 UTC*

## Condition

Durable Function apps using the Azure Storage backend, configured to use a separate storage account (via connectionName/connectionStringName in host.json), hosted on Consumption, Flex Consumption, or Elastic Premium plans, with Target-Based Scaling enabled and not using Runtime-Driven Scaling, may experience improper scaling (delayed/stuck orchestrations) and excessive storage costs due to the Scale Controller querying the default storage account instead of the configured one.

## Diagnostic Query

```kusto
let ST = ago(24h);
let ET = now();
let lookBackWindow = 30d;
let triggerMonitorLogs =
    cluster('wawscus.kusto.windows.net').database('wawsprod').TriggerMonitorLogs
    | union cluster('wawswus.kusto.windows.net').database('wawsprod').TriggerMonitorLogs
    | union cluster('wawseus.kusto.windows.net').database('wawsprod').TriggerMonitorLogs
    | union cluster('wawseas.kusto.windows.net').database('wawsprod').TriggerMonitorLogs
    //| union cluster('wawsweu.kusto.windows.net').database('wawsprod').TriggerMonitorLogs
    | union cluster('wawsneu.kusto.windows.net').database('wawsprod').TriggerMonitorLogs
    | extend component = 'TM';
let scaleControllerLogs =
    All("ScaleControllerEvents")
    | extend component = 'SC';
let allScalingLogs =
    scaleControllerLogs
    | union triggerMonitorLogs
    | project PreciseTimeStamp, Level, AppName = tolower(SiteName), Source, ExceptionType, ExceptionMessage, Message, Details, component;
let appsWithCustomDurableStorageConfigured =
    allScalingLogs
    | where PreciseTimeStamp between (ST - lookBackWindow .. ET)
    | where Message startswith "Successfully added trigger to monitor for site."
    | where Message has 'orchestrationTrigger' or Message has 'entityTrigger'
    | where Message has 'ConnectionName' or Message has 'ConnectionStringName'
    | distinct AppName;
let appsWithCustomDurableStorageUsed =
    allScalingLogs
    | where PreciseTimeStamp between (ST - lookBackWindow .. ET)
    | where Message startswith "Creating DurableTaskTriggersScaleProvider "
    | where Message !endswith "connectionName = 'Storage'"
    | project AppName;
let activeApps =
    cluster('wawseus.kusto.windows.net').database('wawsprod').WawsAn_omgsitefunctionsentity
    | where pdate between (ST - lookBackWindow .. ET)
    | summarize sum(ExecutionCount) by SiteName, Subscription
    | where sum_ExecutionCount > 0
    | project AppName = tolower(SiteName), SubscriptionId = Subscription;
let errors =
    allScalingLogs
    | where PreciseTimeStamp between (ST .. ST + 30min)
    | where Level == 2
    | where Source == "Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Host.Scale.ScaleManager"
    | where ExceptionType == "System.ArgumentNullException"
    | where ExceptionMessage == "Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'value')"
    | where Message startswith "Failed to query scale result for target scaler 'DurableTask-AzureStorage:"
    | where Details startswith "System.Exception : Error: target worker count for 'DurableTask-AzureStorage:"
    | where Details has "System.ArgumentNullException : Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'value')"
    | where Details has "at Newtonsoft.Json.JsonConvert.DeserializeObject(String value,Type type,JsonSerializerSettings settings)"
    | where Details has "at async Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.DurableTask.DurableTaskTargetScaler.GetScaleResultAsync(TargetScalerContext context)"
    | project PreciseTimeStamp, AppName, component;
appsWithCustomDurableStorageConfigured
| join kind=leftanti (appsWithCustomDurableStorageUsed) on AppName
| join kind=innerunique (activeApps) on AppName
| join kind=innerunique (errors) on AppName
| distinct SubscriptionId, AppName, component
| summarize dcount(SubscriptionId), dcount(AppName) // by component
```

## Estimated Time for Action/Resolution

Scale Controller fix completed by May 2, 2025; Trigger Monitor fix completed by May 8, 2025. No more active impact as of May 8, 2025.

## Internal Mitigation Steps

Deploy hotfixes to Scale Controller and Trigger Monitor components. Continue to monitor for false positives and update impact queries to exclude misconfigured or inactive apps. Communicate with support and billing teams regarding refund eligibility for affected customers.

## Customer Mitigation Steps

1. Avoid configuring a separate Durable storage account; use the default Function app storage account if possible. 2. Enable Runtime-Driven Scaling (Runtime Scale Monitoring) for Elastic Premium apps. 3. Move the app to a Standard App Service plan. 4. Disable Target-Based Scaling by setting the TARGET_BASED_SCALING_ENABLED app setting to 0 (resolves storage cost, not scaling). 5. Use a different Durable Functions backend (MSSQL or DTS).

## Root Cause Analysis

A regression introduced with the Scale Controller V3 rollout caused the Durable Functions scaling code to query the default Azure Functions storage account instead of the configured separate storage account. This led to failed Durable queue queries, improper scaling decisions, and excessive (billable) storage transactions. The issue also affected Trigger Monitor for Flex Consumption apps with VNET integration.
